beats.care: In India you can't use a power bank to charge devices during a flight. Keep it in your hand bag, not the overhead bin.
beats.what: A power bank caught fire in an overhead bin on an IndiGo Delhi to Chennai flight on Sunday. It diverted and landed safely in Hyderabad.
beats.why: IndiGo said smoke came from a passenger's device and crew quickly brought it under control.

cards.body: A passenger's video shows people pressing bags against flames in an overhead bin. Crew used an extinguisher. IndiGo said pilots diverted under safety rules, everyone was safe, and an alternate aircraft took passengers on to Chennai.
They hold lithium batteries packed with energy. If damaged, cheap or overheated, they can short-circuit and burn fast. That's why they're banned from checked-in bags too.
cards.title: why do power banks catch fire?

cards.body: Aviation regulator DGCA's rules from January already say power banks must not go in overhead bins, partly because smoke from inside a bag is spotted late.

cards.q: Should airlines check every power bank at the gate?

opts: Their lithium batteries can catch fire
cards.q: Why are power banks a worry on planes?
cards.why: A battery fire in a closed cabin is dangerous, so rules limit how power banks are carried and used.
